<!-- docs-drift-check -->
### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **4** package(s): `@objectstack/client`, `@objectstack/plugin-hono-server`, `@objectstack/plugin-sharing`, `@objectstack/spec`, touching **25** documentable anchor(s). ⚠️ **1** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/spec/authorable-surface/api.json`), so the pages documenting them are **NOT COVERED by this run** — this is not a clean bill of health for those files.

**9** hand-written doc(s) NAME something this change touched and may need an implementation-accuracy re-verification:

- `content/docs/automation/queues-and-assignment-rules.mdx`  _(via objectsUsingQueues (symbol, a field of interface MePermissionsGrants; a method of class OwnershipQueueService; a method of interface IOwnershipQueueService), object_name (literal, a string literal in routedObjects), objectsUsingQueues (literal, a string literal in AnyQueueReader), sys_assignment_rule (literal, a string literal in ASSIGNMENT_RULE_OBJECT))_
- `content/docs/automation/webhooks.mdx`  _(via object_name (literal, a string literal in routedObjects))_
- `content/docs/data-modeling/field-types.mdx`  _(via object_name (literal, a string literal in routedObjects))_
- `content/docs/deployment/cli.mdx`  _(via object_name (literal, a string literal in routedObjects))_
- `content/docs/frontend/plugins/plugin-detail.mdx`  _(via object_name (literal, a string literal in routedObjects))_
- `content/docs/kernel/runtime-services/audit-service.mdx`  _(via object_name (literal, a string literal in routedObjects))_
- `content/docs/permissions/record-view-auditing.mdx`  _(via object_name (literal, a string literal in routedObjects))_
- `content/docs/protocol/kernel/http-protocol.mdx`  _(via object_name (literal, a string literal in routedObjects))_
- `content/docs/protocol/kernel/i18n-standard.mdx`  _(via object_name (literal, a string literal in routedObjects))_

⛔ **3** release-owned page(s) also name something this change touched. These are **read-only**:

- `content/docs/releases/v17/17-6.mdx`  _(via object_name (literal, a string literal in routedObjects))_
- `content/docs/releases/v18/18-3.mdx`  _(via hasAnyQueue (literal, a string literal in AnyQueueReader))_
- `content/docs/releases/v18/18-4.mdx`  _(via IOwnershipQueueService (symbol, a top-level interface), sys_assignment_rule (literal, a string literal in ASSIGNMENT_RULE_OBJECT))_

> `content/docs/releases/` is RELEASE-OWNED (AGENTS.md "Documentation Guardrails"): release
> notes are written centrally at release time, and a code PR that edits them is the exact PR
> that guardrail exists to stop. They are still audited — read-only. If one of them is actually
> wrong, **file an issue** or open a dedicated docs-only PR; do not edit it here.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **1** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/spec/authorable-surface/api.json`) — pages documenting those are invisible to this run
- **1** anchor(s) matched too much of the corpus to be a work list: `organization_id (literal, 41 pages)`
- **2** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **65** of **247** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **182** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **182**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **59** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **123** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **180** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json a34eb0716a8e9838ea286677f305e71df74c62f6` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `5844c02ea3ebe35b67cd1b56a9a353a019402e75` — the merge of head `18bca3ca696c85111a7625f6fe9ec05c44fc051e` into base `a34eb0716a8e9838ea286677f305e71df74c62f6`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 5844c02ea3ebe35b67cd1b56a9a353a019402e75 && git checkout 5844c02ea3ebe35b67cd1b56a9a353a019402e75
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin a34eb0716a8e9838ea286677f305e71df74c62f6 18bca3ca696c85111a7625f6fe9ec05c44fc051e && git checkout -B drift-repro a34eb0716a8e9838ea286677f305e71df74c62f6 && git merge --no-ff 18bca3ca696c85111a7625f6fe9ec05c44fc051e

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json a34eb0716a8e9838ea286677f305e71df74c62f6
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs a34eb0716a8e9838ea286677f305e71df74c62f6` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `549be4bf9bda043e360d966814fb2202896f20e1`
Local-runs: none
Scope: packages/spec/src/api/auth.zod.ts, packages/spec/src/contracts/ownership-queue-service.ts + packages/plugins/plugin-sharing/src/ownership-queue-service.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-hono-server/src/current-user-endpoints.ts, packages/client/src/index.ts, ui/packages/permissions/src/PermissionContext.ts, ui/packages/permissions/src/MePermissionsProvider.tsx, ui/packages/permissions/src/usePermissions.ts, ui/packages/plugin-list/src/ListView.tsx

The brief named head `a342f155624e2afee9005fb6bb247ecef3352ab5`. The head moved to `549be4bf9bda043e360d966814fb2202896f20e1` during the review. I read the delta myself: one commit, one file, `.changeset/34602-queue-toggle-per-object.md` (`@objectstack/spec` patch → minor, `Metadata-protocol: none` → `added`). The code reviewed in ①, ③ and ④ is byte-identical on both heads. This record is for the new head.

Gate state when this record was written (check-runs on `549be4bf`, read 2026-11-17T05:47Z): 18 success, 13 skipped, 20 still in progress, and three runs of `Check Changeset` — one failure and one cancelled, both superseded, and the newest (run 133847434109) success; ② explains them. The 20 in progress include Build Core, Build UI Deps, Test Core 1/8 to 8/8, the Lint and Type Check families and Live E2E UI. Their verdicts were not in when I wrote this, so this record does not vouch for them: the PASS below is the judgment of ① to ④, and any of those runs concluding red on this head overrides it for landing.

### ① Derived judgments

- `MePermissionsAuthenticatedResponseSchema` (strict) gains the required key `objectsUsingQueues: string[]`. The accept-set moves both ways: a body with the key was refused and is now accepted; a body without it was accepted and is now refused. For the served answer this is right: the server sends the key on all three authenticated bodies (full, degraded, closed), so "every key present" on the closed body still holds. Right, with the consumer-side effect named in ② (S2).
- `MePermissionsAnonymousResponseSchema` is untouched: the anonymous body carries no list. Right.
- `IOwnershipQueueService` gains the optional method `objectsUsingQueues?(organizationId)`. An implementation written before it still satisfies the interface, and the route answers `[]` without it. Right.
- `packages/spec/authorable-surface/api.json` gains `api/MePermissionsAuthenticatedResponse:objectsUsingQueues`. A generated baseline that records exactly the one key. Right.
- `@objectstack/client`: a doc-comment change only; the typed answer follows the spec type. Right.
- `@object-ui/permissions`: `PermissionContextValue.objectsUsingQueues?: readonly string[]`, optional, `undefined` = no answer. An additive optional member on a context type. Right.
- `@object-ui/plugin-list`: a new export `objectUsesQueues(list, objectName)`, and the toggle's condition narrows from `hasAnyQueue && objectHasOwnershipQueue` to those two AND membership in the list. This is the narrowing the ruling (6937524209) orders; it removes nothing an author can write. Right.
- Behaviour under version skew (a new console against a server that does not send the key): `objectsUsingQueues` is `undefined`, so the toggle is hidden on every object. This is the fail direction the changeset states ("An answer without the field is treated as no"). Right, and it is a visible change for that pairing.

### ② Semver level

- On the brief's head (`a342f155`) the changeset declared `Metadata-protocol: none` with `@objectstack/spec: patch`, and `Check Changeset` concluded **failure** on it (level axis: `authorable-surface/api.json` moved while the line said `none`). That was a real mismatch. The precedent itself, #28508's changeset `4d278c9`, shipped as `Metadata-protocol: added` in `@objectstack/spec` 18.3.0 *Minor Changes*.
- On this head the changeset and the PR body both read `Clause-②: yes (widening)` and `Metadata-protocol: added`, with `@objectstack/spec: minor` and `patch` on plugin-sharing, plugin-hono-server, client, `@object-ui/permissions` and `@object-ui/plugin-list`. That matches what the diff publishes and the precedent. `Check Changeset` on this head ran three times: 133846352407 failed because it read the PR body before its line was changed (its annotation quotes `Metadata-protocol: none`), 133846651252 was cancelled by the next one, and 133847434109, the newest, concluded **success** at 05:47:49Z.
- `Clause-②: yes (widening)` is the right line for the served answer: the wire gains a key, no key leaves, and every in-tree reader tolerates its absence. I do not read this as the `(narrowing)` arm. Nothing a metadata author can write is refused, and no reader of the response loses anything.
- The required key does narrow one thing, on the consumer side: code that CONSTRUCTS a `MePermissionsAuthenticatedResponse` (a fixture, a mock server, another implementation of the route) no longer type-checks without the key, and a body recorded from an older server no longer parses against the strict schema. About 140 fixtures in this diff changed for exactly that reason. The changeset does not say so. #28508's changeset did carry that sentence for `hasAnyQueue` ("A fixture typed as the response … adds `hasAnyQueue`").

S2 (should-fix) — the changeset should carry one migration sentence for consumers that construct or validate the response type: add `objectsUsingQueues: []` to a fixture typed as the response, and a body from a server older than this release does not parse against the strict schema. The level and the Clause-② arm stay as they are.

### ③ Boundary flags

Dev flags (the report's `deviations`), each answered:

- About 140 UI fixtures and 13 warm-up imports outside the claimed surface: accepted. They follow mechanically from the required key and from `check:test-source-alias`; claim amendment 6939761506 widened the surface to them. They are the lane seat's ACCEPT, not reviewed here.
- `packages/verify` door test, client doc comment and test, the docs paragraph, the generated reference page: accepted, same amendment.
- The PR body's thread link is the thread's own: no contract effect.
- Serial constraint not met (PR #34623 still open): a landing condition, not a review finding. This record is for `549be4bf`; a merge of `origin/main` moves the head and this record does not cover the new one.
- Card bookkeeping: amendment 6939761506 cites "amendment 6937432906", and the amendment on the card is 6937613028. A wrong id in a comment; the seat can correct it.

`open_questions`: empty. `security_findings`: "none" — see ④, where I name the disclosure the field adds; I agree it is within what the ruling asked to be stated, and found no leak beyond it.

`out_of_scope_findings` — "no index on the `queue` column, noted, not filed": answered, and escalated to the seat. "Noted, not filed" leaves the follow-up with no carrier once this PR merges. The seat should file it as a card (an index covering the sitting read, or a measurement on a server database first).

SQL push-down (Prime Directive 5):

- The sitting half is one `find` per candidate object with the whole predicate and `limit 1` in the query (`owner_id` empty, `queue` not empty, the organization). Nothing is materialised in the app and no ids are carried between reads. Each object is its own table, so the engine's object-at-a-time read cannot answer several objects in one statement; a single `UNION ALL` across tables would be a new driver capability, not a pushed-down form of this one. No finding.
- The routed half reads the organization's `recipient_type: 'queue'` rules to completion and takes the distinct `object_name` in the app, filtering `active` and shadowed names there. A `DISTINCT object_name` could push down, but the shadowed-name test needs the registry and the table is the organization's own rule list. No finding.
- The measurement the ruling asked for is in the PR body: 32 reads per call for 31 owned objects, about 10 ms added per permissions read, paid only when `hasAnyQueue` is true. I accept it as answering the condition, with two limits the body itself states and one it does not. Stated: the rig is sqlite-wasm in memory, and "HotCRM-sized" is an estimate. Not stated: the cost is paid on every read of the payload by every user (each sign-in, organization switch and page reload), and the service keeps no memo between calls; "once per session" is per browser session, not per organization. No server-database reading exists. That is why the index follow-up above needs a carrier.

### ④ Design judgment

**`packages/spec/src/api/auth.zod.ts`** — holds against the ruling and the first consumer. The ruling asks for a per-object, server-derived answer beside `hasAnyQueue`, with no authored key; the field is that, and its description states the union (sitting now OR routed), the disclosure bound (objects the caller may read; no queue name, no count) and the staleness. ListView reads it through `usePermissions()` and needs only membership, which a list of names gives. Read against the route:

- "Empty when `hasAnyQueue` is false": the route returns `[]` before asking the service. Agrees.
- "when the ownership-queue service is not registered or cannot answer, and on the closed body": no service, no method, a throw and a non-array all answer `[]`; `closedMePermissionsGrants()` carries `[]`. Agrees.
- "listed only for objects the caller may read": true on the full body (`objects[name].allowRead === true`). On the degraded body the list is NOT narrowed (N2).

**`packages/spec/src/contracts/ownership-queue-service.ts`** — holds against the ruling: one optional method, the same shape as `hasAnyQueue?`. Read sentence by sentence against plugin-sharing's implementation:

- "routed: an organization's `sys_assignment_rule` row, or a declared rule the activation ledger leaves on": agrees, and it matches the assignment engine's own reading in `packages/objectql/src/assignment-rules.ts` (a row under any declared rule's name is not a rule; the same `active` spellings; a declared rule with `active: false` or switched off in the ledger is out). The service is looser than the engine in one direction only: it does not check that the queue a rule names resolves, so a rule naming a missing queue still lists its object. That over-reports towards showing the toggle, which is what the code did everywhere before this change. No finding.
- "Only objects that carry the platform's `queue` column with storage behind it": `resolveInjectedColumnProvenance(def, 'queue') === 'injected-provisioned'`. Agrees, and it is the server-side twin of the console's `objectHasOwnershipQueue`.
- "Resolved under system context; ordered by name": agrees.
- "sitting now: some record of the object, in the organization, has no owner and a queue set": agrees for an object that has the tenant column. It does not hold for one that has not — S1.

S1 (should-fix) — `hasSittingRecord` adds `organization_id: organizationId` to the filter of every candidate object whenever the session has an organization. The `queue` column rides with the owner anchor, not with the tenant column (`resolveInjectedSystemColumns`: `queue = owner`; `tenant` is withheld by `systemFields.tenant: false`, by disabled tenancy and by a platform-global declaration). So a local owned object without `organization_id` is a candidate, and its read names a column the table does not have. The SQL driver refuses such a filter (`unresolvableFilterColumnError`, `packages/drivers/driver-sql/src/sql-driver-read-exit-fault.ts`), the service catches it, warns once and answers `false`. The message says the filter "stays hidden until the read succeeds", and this read never succeeds. The effect: on such an object the toggle is hidden for good even while records sit in a queue, where `main` showed it and the filter worked. It fails in the hidden direction and leaks nothing, and no object in this tree has the combination (the tenant-less objects here are external or `sys_`), so I grade it should-fix. I derived this by reading the three files, not by running it. The fix: add the organization predicate only when the object carries the tenant column, and pin it with a test on a tenant-less owned object.

**`packages/plugins/plugin-sharing/src/ownership-queue-service.ts`** — agrees with the contract apart from S1. The union is built routed-first, so a routed object costs no sitting read. A failed read drops one object and the others still answer. Concurrency is bounded at 8.

N1 (nit) — the comment on `SITTING_READ_CONCURRENCY` calls each read "one indexed `limit 1` read". The PR body says there is no index on `queue`, and the registry gives the injected ownership columns none of their own. Say what the tree says.

**`packages/plugins/plugin-hono-server/src/current-user-endpoints.ts`** — agrees with the schema. Attempts to break it:

- Object names the caller cannot read: on the full body the list is filtered by the served `objects` map, the same map the console is already given, so a name appears only where `allowRead` is already `true`. A disabled package's objects leave that map, so they leave the list too. No leak found.
- What a member does learn: that some record of an object they may read sits in a queue in their organization, or that a rule routes there, even when sharing would hide that record from them. This is the disclosure the ruling asked to be stated against #28508's "Only the boolean", and the PR body and the field description state it. Within the ruling.
- Absent-method path: no service, a service without the method, a throw, a non-array, non-string or empty entries. All answer `[]` or drop the entry; the throw is logged; the permissions body is never lost. Agrees with "the route answers `[]` when the registered service does not carry it".
- Outer catch: the closed body carries `[]`, never the unnarrowed list.

N2 (nit) — the degraded body (no SecurityPlugin) serves the list unnarrowed, and the code comment says why: there is no `objects` map, and the server enforces no object grant there. The schema's sentence "listed only for objects the caller may read" has no such exception. One clause in the description would make the two agree. Related: with `organizationId` null both halves read with no organization filter, so the answer is environment-wide; `hasAnyQueue` has had the same posture since #28508, and the contract's "the objects of `organizationId`" does not say it.

**`packages/client/src/index.ts`** — a doc comment; agrees.

**`ui/packages/permissions/src/{PermissionContext.ts,MePermissionsProvider.tsx,usePermissions.ts}`** — the field is handed on verbatim; `undefined` with no authenticated answer and with no provider. Agrees with "an unknown answer cannot show one does".

**`ui/packages/plugin-list/src/ListView.tsx`** — the first consumer. `queueFilterOffered` is `hasAnyQueue === true` AND `objectUsesQueues(objectsUsingQueues, schema.objectName)` AND `objectHasOwnershipQueue(objectDef)`. An absent list, a non-array and a non-string object name all answer no. The card's acceptance reads off it: an organization with a queue, and an object nothing sits in and no rule routes to, shows no toggle; an object with a parked record or a routing rule shows it. Staleness: the provider refetches on a `requestKey` change or a reload, so a first hand-parked record shows the toggle from the next read; the docs paragraph tells authors this. Holds. The static-markup e2e the card names (`ui/e2e/list-toolbar-view-name-phone.spec.ts`) does not read the permissions answer and is unaffected.

No must-fix. Two should-fix (S1, S2), two nits (N1, N2).

Implemented-by: `claude/project-thread-zu7kjp`
Reviewed-by: `session_01WGufzgh1zkZzDXL36ckWAG`
Security-touching: yes

**VERDICT: PASS**

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `0ea1dd6956a41652e73afaf1ec4d8e5a8e987660`
Local-runs: none
Scope: packages/spec/src/api/auth.zod.ts, packages/spec/src/contracts/ownership-queue-service.ts + packages/plugins/plugin-sharing/src/ownership-queue-service.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-hono-server/src/current-user-endpoints.ts, packages/client/src/index.ts, ui/packages/permissions/src/PermissionContext.ts, ui/packages/permissions/src/MePermissionsProvider.tsx, ui/packages/permissions/src/usePermissions.ts, ui/packages/plugin-list/src/ListView.tsx

This record supersedes the one on `549be4bf9bda043e360d966814fb2202896f20e1` (comment 6939900314). I read the delta myself: two commits (`7253277006`, `0ea1dd6956`), five files — the changeset, `packages/spec/src/api/auth.zod.ts` (description text), the generated `content/docs/references/api/auth.mdx`, plugin-sharing's `ownership-queue-service.ts` and its test. The hono route, the client, the service contract file and the `ui/` files are byte-identical to `549be4bf`, and what the earlier record says of them stands.

Earlier findings on this head:

- S1: closed for the case it named (the read is no longer refused on an object without `organization_id`), but the way it was closed opens M1 below.
- S2: closed. The changeset carries a **Migration** paragraph: a fixture or stub server adds `objectsUsingQueues: []`, and a parse of an older server's body fails on the missing key, with the way round it.
- N1: closed. The comment on `SITTING_READ_CONCURRENCY` now says the `queue` column has no index and a read that finds nothing can scan.
- N2: closed for the degraded body: the schema description now carries the exception ("except on the degraded body, where no object permissions resolved and the list is not narrowed"), and the generated reference page matches it. The null-organization half was a remark, not a request.

Gate state when this record was written (check-runs on `0ea1dd69`, read 2026-11-17T05:59Z): none red. 9 success, among them `Check Changeset`, `Governed Surface Queue Guard`, `PR-body guards` and `Spec property liveness`. 19 still in progress: Build Core, Build Docs, Build UI Deps, Dogfood Regression Gate, the seven Lint families and ESLint, the four Type Check families, Plan Test Core shards, Plan Test UI shards and Live E2E UI; the Test Core shards had not been created yet. This record does not vouch for any of them.

### ① Derived judgments

Unchanged from the earlier record, and each still right: the required key `objectsUsingQueues: string[]` on the strict `MePermissionsAuthenticatedResponseSchema`; the optional `IOwnershipQueueService.objectsUsingQueues?`; the one new key in `authorable-surface/api.json`; the optional member on `PermissionContextValue`; the new export `objectUsesQueues` and the narrowed toggle condition in `ListView`.

New on this head:

- The schema description gains one clause (the degraded-body exception). Description text only; the accept-set does not move. Right.
- `objectsUsingQueues` in plugin-sharing changes which rows it reads for an object with no `organization_id` column: before, a scoped read the driver refused; now, a read with no organization in the filter and none in the context. That is a change to what the served list can name. Wrong for one class of object — M1.

### ② Semver level

- The changeset and the PR body both read `Clause-②: yes (widening)` and `Metadata-protocol: added`; `@objectstack/spec` is `minor`, and plugin-sharing, plugin-hono-server, client, `@object-ui/permissions` and `@object-ui/plugin-list` are `patch`. This matches what the diff publishes and the precedent (#28508's changeset, 18.3.0 *Minor Changes*, `added`). `Check Changeset` concluded success on this head.
- The arm is right: the wire gains a key and loses none. The consumer-side effect of the required key is now stated in the changeset (S2 closed). The migration paragraph is accurate against the tree: the console does not parse the body, and nothing outside `packages/spec` parses with the schema.

### ③ Boundary flags

- The dev's flags and the empty `open_questions` were answered in the earlier record; nothing in this round adds one. Still open for the seat, unchanged: the index follow-up has no card ("noted, not filed"), and the serial constraint (PR #34623 first, then a merge of `origin/main`, which moves the head past this record).
- SQL push-down: unchanged, no finding. The round adds no read. The sitting read still carries its whole predicate and `limit 1` into the query; dropping the organization predicate for a tenant-less object removes a filter, it does not move work into the app.
- Card bookkeeping: claim amendment 6939831560 records the `Metadata-protocol: added` correction. The wrong amendment id I named earlier (6937432906 for 6937613028) is still on the card.

### ④ Design judgment

**`packages/spec/src/api/auth.zod.ts`** — holds. The new clause agrees with the route: on the degraded body the list goes out as the service gave it, and the code comment there gives the same reason. Every other sentence was checked against the route in the earlier record and the route has not changed.
